title: PRD: Hosted API — Contextual Bundles (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) and Launch Readiness Playbook
creator: Lena Park
description: Summary: This PRD defines 'Contextual Bundles' — a hosted-API feature that lets callers atomically request pipelines combining chat/completions with accompanying embeddings and optional rerank steps. Goals: reduce round-trips for context-heavy flows, provide predictable cost/latency tradeoffs, and preserve per-request determinism and evalability. The playbook includes scope, acceptance criteria, QA & eval tasks, rollout strategy, and post-launch observability requirements. Context: several enterprise customers requested single-call retrieval+generation for retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) patterns and multi-step ranking pipelines. This feature must cover chat & completion surfaces, embeddings generation for external indexing, and optional rerank using model-provided scores or internal reranker service.
scope_in_scope: API surface: /v1/contextual-bundles with structured payload that includes: inputs, retrieval references, embedding configs, and rerank instructions
Server-side orchestration that executes: embeddings -> retrieval hook (crediting external retrievals) -> candidate generation (chat/completions) -> optional rerank step
Telemetry: per-stage timing, token counts, unit cost attribution (embedding vs generation vs rerank), and SLO traces
Backward-compatible behavior for existing chat/completions/embeddings endpoints (they remain supported unchanged)
Config flags for deterministic mode, temperature overrides, and max_tokens per candidate
Canary rollout with tenant gating and per-tenant opt-in toggle
out_of_scope: Built-in document store — we will not ship an embedded vector DB; external retrievals are called via configurable webhooks
Complex multi-turn session management beyond a single request/response bundle
Training-time operations or model weight changes
On-prem private deployment packaging for this first launch (Private packaging is tracked in a follow-up ticket)
requirements: API contract (OpenAPI snippet) drafted and reviewed by API team
Server orchestration must expose per-stage identifiers in response for debugging
Prefix/KV caching semantics: generation stage must be able to reuse caches when upstream embeddings & retrieval inputs identical
Cost accounting: bill tokens separately for embeddings, generation, and rerank; UI in Console must attribute cost by stage
SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 600ms for small bundles (<=1k tokens), availability 99.95%
Fallbacks: if rerank service fails, return unranked candidates with a clear diagnostic field; if embeddings fail, abort early with structured error code
Evals: create eval sets for 5 retrieval scenarios and regression checks for deterministic mode
Security: input sanitation and size quotas; ensure webhook retrievals cannot induce SSRF (security review required)
acceptance_criteria: API contract approved and published: sample requests + response schema with examples for chat+embeddings+rerank
End-to-end integration tests pass on staging with synthetic retrieval webhooks (coverage >= 90% paths)
Performance: canary tenants demonstrate <10% median latency regression vs baseline generation-only for equivalent payloads
Telemetry: Console shows per-stage latency and cost breakdown for canary tenants; token accounting matches logs
Determinism: deterministic mode produces byte-for-byte identical outputs for identical requests across two independent runs in staging
Fallback semantics validated: triggered failure modes produce documented error codes and do not crash orchestration
Security sign-off completed: SSRF & input quotas tests green; penetration test findings triaged
Ops runbook in place: rollback steps, tenant throttles, and alert thresholds defined
Canary policy: staged expansion to 10% of production tenants over 7 days with auto-rollback on quality or latency regressions
milestones: 2025-02-18: API schema review with SDK & API teams
2025-03-02: Integration tests & eval harness initial results (this review)
risks: Increased tail latency due to multi-stage orchestration and external retrieval webhooks
Billing confusion if Console does not clearly separate stage costs
Determinism hard to guarantee when relying on external retrieval timings/variants
SSRF or webhook security gaps could cause customer data exposure or abuse
Edge-case combinatorics: many optional flags may create untested code paths
mitigations: Add request-level timeouts and staged parallelism where safe; provide 'fast-fail' config for retrieval stage
Console team to ship a temporary breakdown view in the canary dashboard before GA
Implement request hashing and normalized retrieval payload for deterministic mode; capture retrieval fingerprints
Require signed webhook contracts + allowlist per-tenant; security gating before canary
Limit initial feature flags to a small, reviewed subset and expand after evaluative rollout
qa_checklist: Unit tests for orchestration logic and error paths
Integration tests with mocked retrieval webhooks and with an internal reranker service
Load tests: synthetic bundles at 1k QPS equivalent to validate batching behavior
Determinism regression run: 1000 identical requests across 3 staging nodes
Manual exploratory: Console UX for bundle inspection, logs, and trace links
Security tests: SSRF fuzzing, quota exhaustion, and payload injection
rollout_plan: Canary phase 1: 3 internal tenants + 2 trusted customers (opt-in) for 72 hours
Canary phase 2: 5% of tenants for 7 days with automated metric checks (latency, error rate, quality via eval harness)
Progressive expansion: 25% -> 50% -> 100% across 2-week windows subject to health gates
Rollback: immediate global rollback to disable orchestration and fallback to stage-by-stage guidance if error rate > 1% or latency 95p > 2x baseline
